# Instagram Reel Dopamine Storytelling

## What This Skill Produces
This skill creates a complete Instagram Reel script designed for high retention and action.

Output includes:
- Hook line options for first 1-3 seconds
- Timestamped reel script
- Visual direction per beat (shot idea + on-screen text)
- Caption with CTA
- One pinned-comment idea

## When to Use
Use this skill when you need:
- A stronger opening hook to reduce early drop-off
- A story-driven script instead of a flat informational script
- Better engagement through curiosity, emotion, and reward pacing
- Reels that connect founder journey, product proof, and conversion
- Phase A (hype/tease), Phase B (launch week), or Phase C (post-launch social proof) content

## SanskaTots Brand Context
Before writing any script, lock these facts in:

**Core selling idea:** You are not selling books. You are selling a feeling — *"Finally, something Indian for my Indian child."* Every line must make an Indian mom nod, laugh, cry, or share.

**Brand tagline:** Indian Roots. Curious Minds.

**Primary audience:** Indian moms, 25–40, urban Tier 1 & 2 cities, screen-time conscious, culture-proud.

**Phase 1 product lineup (7 books):**
- 3 Velcro Activity / Busy Books (All In One Busy Book, Montessori Busy Book, one more)
- 2 Mythology Books (BhagavadGita for Kids, Ramayana Stories)
- 2 Educational Books

**Brand voice:** Casual Indian English — the way Indian moms actually talk. No forced slang, no corporate feel. Just desi warmth. Every script must sound spoken, not written. Hinglish is only used when explicitly requested.

**Three content phases:**
- Phase A (Hype & Tease): Build anticipation, product reveals, FOMO before launch
- Phase B (Launch Week): Countdown, launch day urgency, first orders
- Phase C (Post-Launch): Social proof, reviews, combo offers, repeat purchase push

## Required Inputs
Collect these before writing:
- Content pillar: Humor & Relatable / Emotional-Founder Story / Education-Parenting Tips / Product Showcase / Cultural Pride / Behind the Scenes
- Emotional sales trigger: which of the 5 triggers to use (see below)
- Content phase: Phase A (hype) / Phase B (launch) / Phase C (post-launch)
- Core story event or product feature: specific and real
- Duration: 20-30s, 30-45s, or 45-60s
- Voice: English (default) / Hinglish / Hindi

If any input is missing, ask short clarifying questions before writing.

## 5 Emotional Sales Triggers (SanskaTots)
Every reel must use exactly one of these:

| Trigger | How It Works | Best Product |
|---|---|---|
| GUILT → RELIEF | Activate guilt the parent already carries (screen time, ignoring culture), then show the product as emotional relief | All In One Busy Book, Velcro Books |
| FEAR OF MISSING OUT | Show other kids / moms already using it. Create urgency. | Any — especially launch week |
| PRIDE / IDENTITY | Make buying = being a good Indian parent. Connect to culture, heritage. | BhagavadGita for Kids, Mythology Books |
| COMPARISON SHOCK | Show the clear gap between cheap/generic and SanskaTots quality or durability | Montessori Busy Book |
| CHILD JOY | Genuine child reaction — nothing sells faster. Parent's brain screams "I want that for MY kid." | All books, especially demos |

## 6 Content Pillars (Posting Mix)
Every reel belongs to one pillar. Keep this mix across all content:

| Pillar | Goal | Target Mix |
|---|---|---|
| Humor & Relatable | Shares, reach, new followers | 30% |
| Emotional / Founder Story | Loyalty, trust, DMs | 25% |
| Education / Parenting Tips | Authority, saves | 20% |
| Product Showcase | Conversions, Amazon clicks | 15% |
| Cultural Pride | Identity, NRI audience, shares | 7% |
| Behind the Scenes | Authenticity, community | 3% |

## Six Levels Of The Dopamine Ladder
Use all six levels in sequence unless duration is very short.

1. Pattern Interrupt
- Break expectation in first 1-3 seconds.
- Use bold contrast, surprising claim, or unresolved tension.

2. Curiosity Gap
- Reveal enough to pull attention, but hold back the full answer.
- Phrase as a mystery or challenge in progress.

3. Relatable Tension
- Show the struggle the audience already feels.
- Keep it concrete (budget, time, confusion, fear of failure).

4. Progress Reward
- Deliver mini wins or visible movement.
- Show action snippets, proof, or before/after progress.

5. Identity Payoff
- Let viewers feel "this is me" or "I can do this too".
- Connect outcome to their self-image or aspiration.

6. Action Release
- End with one clear next step.
- Use a single CTA: comment, DM, save, follow, or click bio.

## 6 Hook Types (Use One Per Reel)
Choose the hook type that fits the content pillar and trigger:

1. **Pattern Interrupt** — Say or show something contrary to popular belief or visually unexpected in the first 2 seconds. *"Giving my kid the most expensive toy every day. Also me: hiding ₹299 book under the bed."*
2. **Curiosity Gap** — Give an incomplete fact or result, hold back the reveal until the end. *"I made this mistake when choosing my toddler's first book..."*
3. **Relatable Pain** — Name the exact struggle the audience already feels. *"No Indian mom should have to beg her 3-year-old to sit still for 5 minutes."*
4. **Micro-Story** — Dive straight into a raw, personal narrative — no setup, no polish. *"Day 1 of starting SanskaTots. ₹0 budget. No idea what we were doing."*
5. **Comparison (This vs That)** — Show a clear side-by-side contrast to demonstrate value. *"iPad reaction vs. Velcro book reaction. Watch the difference."*
6. **Visual Hook** — Arrest attention with a visually unexpected action in the first 3 seconds — velcro rip, zoom into illustration, unboxing reveal, child reaction close-up.

---

## CTA Bank (Always Pick Exactly One)
Rotate these across reels. Never use more than one CTA per reel:
- "Link in bio — Amazon delivery in 1-2 days"
- "Comment 'BOOK' and I'll DM you the link"
- "Save this for when you need 30 minutes of peace"
- "Tag a mom who NEEDS this"
- "Which book should I show next? Comment below"
- "This is selling fast — grab yours before it's gone"
- "Follow for the next chapter of this story"
- "Set a reminder — launching June 1st on Amazon"

---

## Writing Procedure
1. Choose content pillar, emotional sales trigger, and content phase.
2. Choose one hook type.
3. Choose one emotional arc: struggle-to-win, myth-to-truth, or challenge-to-proof.
4. Draft 3 hook line options using the chosen hook type.
5. Map the script to the six dopamine levels.
6. Add timestamps and keep each beat concise.
7. Add visual instructions for every beat:
   - Camera action and scene context
   - On-screen text
   - Audio note (ASMR velcro, trending audio, voiceover)
8. Pick one CTA from the CTA bank.
9. Write caption and pinned comment.
10. Run all quality checks before finalizing.

## Branching Logic

**By content phase:**
- Phase A (Hype & Tease): Use Curiosity Gap or Visual hook. Trigger: FOMO. CTA: save or follow.
- Phase B (Launch Week): Use Pattern Interrupt or Comparison. Trigger: GUILT→RELIEF or CHILD JOY. CTA: Amazon link or Comment 'BOOK'.
- Phase C (Post-Launch): Use Micro-Story or Relatable Pain. Trigger: PRIDE/IDENTITY or COMPARISON SHOCK. CTA: Tag a mom or DM link.

**By content pillar:**
- Humor & Relatable: Lead with relatable pain hook. Keep Level 3 long, compress Levels 4 and 5.
- Emotional / Founder Story: Use micro-story hook. Expand Level 5 (identity payoff).
- Product Showcase: Use visual hook. Expand Level 4 (proof). CTA must link directly to Amazon.
- Cultural Pride: Use identity language throughout Levels 3 and 5. CTA: share or tag.
- Education / Parenting Tips: Use curiosity gap hook. End with save CTA.
- Behind the Scenes: Use micro-story hook. Raw and unpolished tone preferred.

**By duration:**
- 20-30s: Compress Levels 3 and 5 to one sentence each.
- 30-45s: Full six levels with one proof beat.
- 45-60s: Add one extra proof beat inside Level 4.

**By audience temperature:**
- Cold audience: Skip jargon. Add one-line brand context before Level 3.
- Warm audience: Skip brand intro. Move directly to tension and proof.

## Quality Criteria (Completion Checks)
A script is complete only if ALL checks pass:
- Hook appears in first 1-3 seconds and creates interruption.
- One and only one emotional sales trigger is active throughout the script.
- Each dopamine level is present and in sequence.
- No generic lines like "hard work" or "Indian values" without a specific scene.
- At least one concrete proof moment exists (child reaction, velcro sound, real stat, or side-by-side).
- CTA is singular, explicit, and from the CTA bank — not multiple asks.
- Brand voice check: script sounds like casual Indian English, not formal or corporate.
- Cultural reference or product name is used naturally — not forced.
- Final read-aloud test: sounds spoken, not essay-like.
- Content pillar is clear from the first 5 seconds.
